newsitem.title: USA: Kawasaki unit sues three rivals in patent dispute.
newsitem.headline: Kawasaki unit sues three rivals in patent dispute.

text.p: LNP Engineering Plastics Inc, a unit of Kawasaki Steel Corp, has sued three competitors alleging they infringed three LNP patents for fibre reinforced compositions and the methods for producing them.

Lighter weight computer housings are among the products made with the patented technology, known as long fiber reinforced thermoplastic, or LFRT. According to the records of the U.S. District Court in Delaware, LNP filed separate but related suits against Miller Waste Mills Inc, DSM Engineering Plastics and Hoechst Celanese Corp/Polymer Composites Inc.
DSM Engineering was formed in January when DSM NV merged its Polymer Corp unit with Sheffield Plastics Inc. DSM Engineering is based in Evansville, Indiana.
Polymer Composite is a unit of Hoechst Celanese Corp, an affiliate of Hoechst AG. Hoechst Celanese is the fifth largest chemical company in North America.
LNP alleged the defendants were "diverting to (themselves) customers who would otherwise purchase LFRT from LNP at the prices charged by LNP."
LNP produces fibers reinforced with glass and carbon fiber and also lubricants, in the Netherlands and the UK.
